title: Closing the Loop
summary: Linked automations = one customer journey + data that informs Analyst decisions

sections.heading: Orientation — Beginning of the Lesson
sections.subtitle: Beginning of the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** Powerful separate automations — but when linked in a **Customer Journey**, they become a system.
- **Why now?** After gathering leads, WhatsApp responses, and follow-ups, you need the complete picture, not just each part alone.
- **What after the lesson?** You will map the journey from start to finish, from lead to follow-up.

sections.heading: Tension — A Familiar Situation
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Everything works — but there is no complete picture.
- You have a form capturing leads. WhatsApp responds. Follow-ups send messages. Each one works.
- But you don't know: Which channel brings in the best leads? Which follow-up message gets the most responses? Where does the customer get stuck?
- Separate automations without connection = a lot of work without learning. Connecting generates data — and data leads you to the **Analyst** path.

sections.heading: Core Idea — One Journey = Lead → Response → Follow-up → Data
sections.subtitle: One Journey = Lead → Response → Follow-up → Data
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Lead capture:** Grabs attention and records it.
- **WhatsApp / Instant Response:** Serves the customer confidently.
- **Follow-up:** Continues the conversation if it goes silent.
- Every step is recorded: Source, Time, Channel, Response, Conversion. This is what the **Analyst** reads.

sections.heading: Comparison — Separate Islands vs. Connected Journey
sections.subtitle: Separate Islands vs. Connected Journey
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Separate Automations | One Customer Journey |
|---------------------|---------------------|
| The form works, WhatsApp works, follow-up works — but there is no map. "What was useful?" — No answer. | Lead from ad → Registration → WhatsApp response → Follow-up on days 2 and 5 → Conversion or closure. Every step is recorded — you can ask and improve. |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms for Connection
sections.subtitle: Two Terms for Connection
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| **Customer Journey** | The complete path from initial interest to follow-up or purchase — not just one step | Ad → Form → Welcome → Follow-up → Sales Call |
| **Feedback Loop** | The data recorded by the automation returns to inform you what can be improved | "Follow-up on day 2 on WhatsApp opened 40% responses — day 5 email opened 10%" |

sections.contentMarkdown: Each stage feeds into the next and records data. **The connected journey** = questions that the **Analyst** will answer.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Question:** You have leads from 3 channels and follow-up is working — but you don't know which channel brings in customers who buy. What is the best question to ask the data?

- **Correct answer:** **Which channel brought in leads that purchased at the highest rate?**
- **Explanation:** **The connected journey** allows you decision questions — not just counting. Channel + conversion = **Analyst**.

sections.heading: Mission — Map the Journey from Lead to Follow-up
sections.subtitle: Map the Journey from Lead to Follow-up
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** The mission is a journey map — not a technical audit. Connect what you learned: Capture, Response, Follow-up — in one customer path. No real numbers are needed — just 5-6 stages + one **Analyst** question.

**Submission:** Lead source · Stages 1-4 (Capture, Response, Follow-up, End) · One **Analyst** question · Sentence: What was missing before the connection?

**Evaluation Criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Connected Journey | 60% | 5 linked stages — not separate automations |
| Analyst Bridge | 40% | One decision question based on journey data |

sections.heading: Confidence Close
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **You understood:** Linked automations = **Customer Journey** + data for improvement.
- **You can:** You have a map from start to finish, from lead to follow-up.
- **Next:** The **Analyst** path — you read the data generated by your system and make better decisions. (End of the Automator path — go back to the map and choose **Analyst**.)
